clue.text: Fruit salad

parts.note: surface reading: a bowl of chopped mixed fruit served as a dessert
setter's reading: a salad made from something that is botanically a fruit though eaten as a vegetable

explanation.walkthrough: Botanically this salad staple is a fruit, so a salad of it is a 'fruit salad' in a very literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists class it as a berry, yet cooks treat it as a vegetable and slice it into green salads.

clue.text: Drunken teens endlessly abounding on resort island

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order
without an end, so the final letter of the word before is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing its last letter
rife means plentiful, abounding

explanation.surface: Boozy teenagers swarm over a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands, a popular Spanish holiday destination for sun-seeking tourists.

clue.text: In conversation, Damon is keen on Spanish performers

indicators.note: conversation is spoken, so the words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: Damon is the actor Matt Damon, and to be keen on something is to adore it

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that the actor Damon has a soft spot for Spanish entertainers.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon stands for his first name, Matt; said quickly, 'Matt adores' runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Matadors are the bullfighters who perform the kill in a Spanish bullring before crowds.

clue.text: 'Buoyant Eel Thief', unusual Booker winner

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the quoted letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the fifteen letters of the quoted phrase are the fodder

explanation.surface: An oddly titled book, 'Buoyant Eel Thief', is said to have won the Booker.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the fodder look like a title; the real title is hidden in its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Hollinghurst's novel won the Man Booker Prize for fiction in 2004.

clue.text: Catching chum? Bait is unnecessary

indicators.note: something caught up gets tangled and snarled, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: chum is fishing slang for bait, but here the two words simply supply letters

explanation.surface: An angler is told that bait isn't needed to catch chum.
explanation.walkthrough: Chum is ground fish thrown in the water to attract a catch, which makes the fishing picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit much means it is excessive or uncalled for, going further than needed.

clue.text: Bowled over by two names for old capital

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
N is the abbreviation for name, taken twice

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed by a pair of names for a former capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' reads as one phrase meaning amazed, but it splits into two cricket abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonn was the seat of government of West Germany until reunification moved it to Berlin.

clue.text: Art event that Serena wasn't in time for?

definitions.text: Art event that Serena wasn't in time for?

parts.words: Art event that Serena wasn't in time for?
parts.note: surface reading: a gallery opening the tennis star Serena Williams arrived late for

parts.words: Art event that Serena wasn't in time for?
parts.note: setter's reading: a famous painting whose title names an event before Serena was born, since her sister Venus is older

explanation.walkthrough: Venus Williams is Serena's older sister, so Serena could not have been around when her sister was born; the art is Botticelli's painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Botticelli's Renaissance masterpiece in the Uffizi shows the goddess arriving ashore on a scallop shell.

clue.text: Fantastic to unwind, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: to unreel is to unwind line or film from a spool

explanation.surface: Someone says it's fantastic to relax and unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwind' suggests relaxing, but here it means letting out line from a reel.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreal is slang for amazing or incredible, so it matches fantastic in its enthusiastic sense.

clue.text: Shock: describing most of the bible as cobblers

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a shock is a thick mop of hair
the Old Testament makes up the larger part of the Christian bible

explanation.surface: It's a shock to hear most of the bible dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, from rhyming slang for something rude; it has nothing to do with shoemakers here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for empty talk and rubbish that should not be believed.

clue.text: Headbanger?

parts.note: surface reading: a heavy-metal fan, or slang for a crazy person
setter's reading: someone who bangs their head into another person's face in a fight

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to 'nut' someone is to headbutt them, and a crazy person is also called by the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for a wild or crazy person, and the answer also suggests one who headbutts.

clue.text: Runs obtained by English in cricket, perhaps with no-one watching

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pieces go within the last

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect, as 'perhaps' flags
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Runs are scored by an English batsman in a cricket match with no spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the chirping creature, not the bat-and-ball game the runs suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something privately, unseen by others, is doing it secretly, out of sight of any observer.

clue.text: Men I see struggling?

indicators.note: the struggling words writhe about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone watches a group of men locked in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the men you see fighting against you.
explanation.definitionFit: Foes are people you fight against, so men seen struggling with you are your opponents.

clue.text: Clumsy tragedian, not a star

indicators.note: clumsy handling knocks things out of place, so the letters are reordered
not a tells us one letter A is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, an actor of tragic roles

explanation.surface: An awkward tragic actor is no star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' at the end looks like a theatrical compliment, but it is the definition in its astronomical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool, luminous star in a late stage of its life cycle.

clue.text: Four admitted to surrealist festival

indicators.note: someone admitted to a place is let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Salvador Dalí was the best-known surrealist painter
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people are let into a festival of surrealist art.
explanation.definitionFit: Divali, also spelt Diwali, is the Hindu festival of lights held in autumn.

clue.text: Biblical character, fellow apparently lasting forever

parts.note: Onan is a son of Judah in Genesis
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man from the Bible seems to live for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on and on seems endless, continuing tediously without stopping.

clue.text: Make little 'uns surround chaps with flowers

parts.note: to forge is to make, as a smith does

indicators.note: to surround is to go all round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: tots are small children
chaps are men

explanation.surface: An instruction to have children gather round some men holding flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: These small blue-flowered plants of the genus Myosotis are named as tokens of remembrance.

clue.text: Impose second of levies on North Carolina fish

indicators.note: second of points to the letter in position two of the next word

parts.note: the second letter of levies
NC is the US state abbreviation for North Carolina
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A tax is placed on the fish caught in North Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the earlier pieces above the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude on someone's rights or time, imposing on them unwelcome.

clue.text: Evening of fun with squeeze, getting into a kiss? Not half

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so one piece is placed within another
not half means half the word is missing, so the back two letters are cut

parts.note: taken as written
to press is to squeeze
taken as written, then cut in half

explanation.surface: A fun night out with a girlfriend, ending in a hug and a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeeze' looks like a boyfriend or girlfriend here, but it is a verb. Après-ski is the socialising after a day on the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the drinking and partying at a ski resort once the day's skiing is over.

clue.text: PM having shag and a lie-down

parts.note: p.m. marks the hours after noon
shag is a long rough pile on cloth, and nap is the raised pile of a fabric

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister enjoys a romp and then a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: PM reads as Prime Minister and shag as British slang for sex; really they are the time of day and the pile of a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sleep taken after lunch is a midday rest, a lie-down in the early part of the day.

clue.text: Some writhe besottedly in old city

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the run starts inside the first word and ends inside the second

explanation.surface: Some lovers squirm about infatuated in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt, and also a city state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Lover's ravished you

indicators.note: ravished means violently seized and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A romantic declaration: your lover has swept you off your feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often call the person doing the puzzle 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The person working on this puzzle is the one reading the clue, addressed directly by the setter.

clue.text: President to be suspended, admitting nothing

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to hover is to hang in the air
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A president is about to be suspended from office, having confessed nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspended' suggests removal from office; it means hanging in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Hoover was the 31st President of the United States, in office from 1929 to 1933.

clue.text: Opposite number in disguise, seen intermittently

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the next

parts.note: a cover is a disguise for a spy
N is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A spy's opposite number in disguise is spotted only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposite number' reads as a counterpart, but 'Opposite' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The converse of a statement is its reverse, so as a noun it means the contrary.

clue.text: Booze cruise: case of white? Not quite

indicators.note: a case holds something inside it, so the letters sit within the words before

parts.note: the run straddles the space between the two words

explanation.surface: On a booze cruise, someone has a case of white wine, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of white' looks like a dozen bottles of wine; it splits into the hidden signal and part of the definition. A booze cruise is a ferry trip to France to buy cheap alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow shade like unbleached linen, an off-white colour.

clue.text: Left … left … voila! Cubs assembled shelters

indicators.note: assembled means put together from parts, so the letters are built into a new order
left in the sense of departed, so a letter goes away from the words after

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the letters of the two words, from which one letter goes

explanation.surface: A scout leader drills the cubs, left, left, then shows off the tents they put up.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'left' sounds like a marching call; the first gives a letter and the second says that letter departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivouac is a temporary camp or makeshift shelter, often without tents, used by soldiers or climbers.

clue.text: Home with tatty walls, heartless relatives

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: tatty means shabby and in disrepair, so the letters are knocked out of order
without a heart, so the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its centre

explanation.surface: A shabby house with peeling walls, owned by uncaring family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Your spouse's parents and siblings are relations by marriage rather than by blood.

clue.text: Special sci-fi device that's used by Banksy

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing used, a noun

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
a ray gun is the classic weapon of science fiction

explanation.surface: Banksy is said to wield a special science-fiction gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy is the anonymous British street artist known for stencilled graffiti.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti artists apply paint with an aerosol or compressed-air tool to cover walls quickly.

clue.text: For starters, I'll serve this halloumi marinated in strips

indicators.note: starters come first in a meal, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.words: I'll serve this halloumi marinated in
parts.note: the initial letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A cook announces a starter of marinated halloumi cut into strips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strips' looks like how the cheese is sliced; it is the definition, strips of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow neck of land joining two larger landmasses; this is its Latin plural.
